title: Applying a decoded transition record
statement: Let $M$ be a coded machine, let $\alpha$ and $x$ be bit strings, let $s$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$, and let $a$ be a one-step action for $M$. For any natural numbers $\mathit{oldp}$ and $p$, one step of the universal interpreter from the evaluation configuration based on the simulation checkpoint of $s$ at cursor $\mathit{oldp}$, in the record-application control state carrying the eight bits of $a$ and the flag indicating whether $a$ halts, with table $M$’s canonical serialization at cursor $p$ and the successor state’s unary tape (using state index $0$ if $a$ halts) at cursor $1$, equals the simulation checkpoint of the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $s$, at table cursor $p$.
hypotheses_covered: $s$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $x$
replaced:
Let $M$ be a coded machine, $\alpha$ a code string, $s$ a configuration of
$M$'s one-work-tape form on an input $x$, and $a$ a transition action of
$M$.  One step of the table interpreter from the evaluation configuration
over the interpreter checkpoint of $s$ (at an arbitrary table cursor) whose
control is the record-application phase carrying the eight fixed bits of
$a$ and the flag recording whether $a$ halts, whose table is the canonical
serialization of $M$ at a cursor $p$, and whose state tape is the intact
unary encoding of $a$'s successor index ($0$ when $a$ halts) with state
cursor $1$, is exactly the interpreter checkpoint of the configuration
obtained by applying $a$ to $s$, with table cursor $p$.
